intro: Slack for founders on Mac is a daily loop: catch up, search old decisions, start a huddle, write the reply, and move on. The fastest route uses a handful of Mac shortcuts, a few menu paths, and a clear view of your plan limits. This page covers those steps, and shows where Lazur helps by voice when you need a hand.
tldr: Slack for founders on Mac is a loop: catch up, search, huddle, write, and decide. Shortcuts cover most of it.
The Free plan keeps 90-day searchable history, so save key decisions in a canvas or doc as well as in threads.
Group huddles, canvas templates, and conditional workflows depend on your plan. Check Slack's pricing page before you build a routine around them.
Lazur points at controls, guides multistep clicks, dictates with fn, and drafts text. It never clicks for you.

blocks.text: What founders do in Slack on Mac every day

Most founders use Slack for four jobs. They catch up on what happened while they were in calls. They answer customers and investors. They make decisions inside threads. They look up what was decided last month. Each job has a faster route on a Mac.
Slack for Mac is a desktop app, and the shortcuts follow Mac habits. ⌘ does most of the work, and ⇧ adds a second layer. If you already live in Mail or Notes, the habits carry over.

Press ⌘ , to open the keyboard shortcuts panel. Slack's help page lists shortcuts for huddles, canvases, and search. It lists no shortcut for sending a message or creating a workflow. Do not waste time hunting for one.
Catch up on Slack on Mac in the right order
Start with what needs you. Press ⌘G and type your name. Mentions show the threads where someone is waiting on you. Then check direct messages. Only after that should you scan the channels you follow.
The common mistake is reading channels from the top. The urgent question sits at the bottom of a busy channel. It waits there while you read about the office coffee order.

items: Search your name with ⌘G and open each thread that tags you.
Answer direct messages from customers, investors, and your co-founder first.
Open the customer or investor channel you watch most closely.
Leave the general channel for the end of the day.

blocks.text: Here is a worked example. You come out of a sales call with a list of open questions. Search the prospect's company name with ⌘G. You find a thread where a teammate already answered half of them. You reply to the rest, then move on. That check usually takes less time than reading the channel from the top.
Search Slack on Mac for old decisions without losing them
Search is ⌘G. Use it when a teammate asks what you agreed to in a thread last month. Scrolling works for the last few hours. It fails after that.

Search matters more than most founders expect. Glean, which sells enterprise search, commissioned a Harris Poll that was published in 2022. It found employees spend at least two hours a day, or 25% of their work week, looking for documents or information. The figure is self-reported and comes from a vendor, so treat it as a rough signal, not a measurement.

The Free plan keeps messages searchable for 90 days. That is short for a company with a long history. Upgrading gives access to the previous 12 months, according to Slack's pricing page. Check your plan before you assume a decision is gone.
Two habits fix most of the problem. Save decisions in a canvas or a doc, with the date in the title. When a search fails, try a person's name and one word from the topic, not the whole sentence.

Say an investor asks what you promised about the pilot price in the spring. Search for the word pilot with ⌘G, add the channel name, then open the oldest match. If that message falls outside your plan's search window, ask the teammate who posted the original doc.
Start huddles and canvases with the right Mac shortcuts
⌘⇧H starts, joins, leaves, or ends a huddle. Use it instead of hunting for a button on a busy morning. ⌘⇧Space mutes or unmutes while you are in a huddle. Press it before you step away from the desk.
⌘⇧N creates a new canvas. A canvas works well for a weekly plan, a fundraising checklist, or a launch brief that the team edits together.

Start from a template when you can. On desktop, click Files in the sidebar, then New in the top right, then Canvas templates. Search or pick a template, preview it, and click Use Template. Slack's article covers desktop only.
Canvas templates need a paid plan, according to the same help article. They apply to all members except Frontline Members. Check your seat before you plan a kickoff around one.

Huddles on the Free plan are limited to 1:1. A founding team that wants a group call needs to check the pricing page first. Do not build a routine around a group huddle until you confirm your plan supports it.
Build a workflow for the founder tasks you repeat
Workflows handle repeat work. A weekly update, a support intake, or a hiring request can run the same steps every time. Start with a standard template instead of a blank build.
Open Agents & tools in the sidebar. If you do not see it, try Tools, then More. Choose Workflows > Templates, pick one, click Set Up, fill in each blue input, and click Publish Workflow.
Who can use a workflow matters. By default, all Full Members can create workflows. Members and guests can use published workflows. Workflow managers can be added or removed after you publish.
Pick a weekly status template that asks for the same few fields each week. Fill in the fields once, read them back, then publish. Your team finds the form in the same place every week.
Read each input before you click Publish Workflow. A blank or wrong field goes out exactly as entered. Editing after publishing is possible, but the first version is what people see.
Workflow Builder limits to check before you build
Conditional branching lives in Workflow Builder and needs the Business+ or Grid plan. Each branch can hold up to ten custom rules. A branch can also include a fallback path for when no rule matches.

Advanced templates open in Workflow Builder. Slack's help page says advanced templates are available on paid plans. It does not say whether standard templates have the same gate. Check the pricing page before you assume either way.
Edge case: a branch with no matching rule and no fallback leaves the flow with nowhere to go. Add a fallback every time. It takes a minute and saves you from a silent break.
Test a new flow in a private channel before you share it with the team. Watch what happens when the answers are blank, odd, or out of order. Those are the cases a founder tends to skip.

blocks.text: Per user pricing is the number to watch. Every full seat on a paid plan adds the per user price. Count the people who need full access before you upgrade, not after.
The Free plan's 10 app limit matters too. Each app you connect uses one of your slots. Keep the ones you open every day, such as your calendar and your support inbox, and drop the rest.
Dictate replies and updates with fn
Hold fn to dictate clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app. Slack is one of those apps. Use dictation for the reply you keep postponing, or for the update that needs a few paragraphs.

Snippets save text you repeat, such as your calendar link or your sign-off. A personal dictionary helps with product names, customer names, and terms that speech tools often mishear. Clipboard slots keep a few items ready to paste.

The main mistake is the cursor. Dictated text lands wherever the cursor sits. Click into the message box first, then hold fn. To see how your speaking pace compares with typing, try the [speaking vs typing test](/tools/speaking-vs-typing-test).
Ask Lazur about the Slack thread on screen
Hold ⌥ ⌘ to ask about anything on screen. Lazur answers out loud. Lazur looks at your screen only while you hold the shortcut, so keep the thread open and visible when you ask.

Good questions for Slack sound like this. What is this customer asking? What is blocking the decision in this thread? Which message needs my answer first? Lazur reads what is on screen and answers from it.

Ask for a draft when you need one. Say something like: draft a reply that confirms Friday and asks for the signed contract. Lazur drafts and types text. Read the draft, change what needs changing, then press Return yourself.
Lazur does not send messages for you. It does not click Send. That step stays with you, which is also the point, since a draft written in a hurry should get one more look.
Where Lazur helps and where it stops

Lazur points at controls, guides multistep tasks, answers questions, dictates, and drafts text. It does not click buttons, edit files, or operate other apps for you. It is not a plugin or add-in for Slack or any other app.

Ask where a control is, and Lazur draws a circle and a label around it on screen. Ask how to finish a task with several steps, and Lazur guides one click at a time, waiting for each click before it moves on.

Privacy matters when a Slack thread holds customer details. Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer them. They are not stored, and content is never used to train AI models.

You can try Lazur without a credit card. Get the Mac app from the [download page](/download). Compare plans on the [pricing page](/pricing). The [Slack page](/apps/slack) shows more examples for this app.
A Monday in Slack on Mac, step by step
Here is a typical start to a week for a founder who runs a small team. Every step uses a shortcut or a menu path from this page, plus Lazur where it saves time.

items: Press ⌘G and search your name. Open each thread that tags you.
Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur which thread needs a decision first.
Hold fn and dictate a short plan for the week into your team channel.
Open Agents & tools, then choose Workflows > Templates, and start the weekly update workflow.
Click Files, then New, then Canvas templates, and open the planning canvas before your first huddle.
Press ⌘⇧H to start the huddle. Press ⌘⇧Space when you step away to mute.

blocks.text: The sequence is short because each step handles one job. Skip any step that does not fit your week. The point is a repeatable order, not a perfect one.
Mistakes founders make in Slack on Mac

items: Reading every channel in order instead of sorting by who needs you.
Assuming an old message is gone without checking the 90-day Free limit.
Building a workflow before you check which plan includes the feature.
Looking for a shortcut to send a message. Slack's help page lists none.
Dictating into the wrong window because the cursor sat somewhere else.
Keeping a decision only in a thread. Copy the result into a canvas or doc.

blocks.text: Each mistake costs a little time. Together they cost a lot of attention. Fix the one that happens most in your week first.
Menu names change, so check your version
Slack ships Mac updates often. The latest build we could confirm is 4.53.280, dated November 3, 2026. That release was a security update with no feature or menu changes.

The workflow help now starts from Agents & tools. Older guides may say Tools. If the names on your screen differ, trust what you see over any guide, this one included. Ask Lazur to circle the sidebar item when you cannot find it.
What to do next

items: Check Slack's pricing page at slack.com/pricing for search history, huddle rules, and template access.
Practice ⌘G, ⌘⇧H, ⌘⇧Space, and ⌘⇧N once each this week.
Build one canvas from a template and one workflow from a template.
Try Lazur on a real thread. Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask what needs an answer first.

faq.question: Is there a separate Slack app for founders on Mac?
faq.answer: No. Founders use the same Slack for Mac desktop app as everyone else. The useful part is choosing the features that match your routine: search, huddles, canvases, and workflows. This page shows which shortcuts and menu paths fit those jobs.

faq.question: What is the fastest way to search Slack on Mac?
faq.answer: Press ⌘G to open search, then type a name, a channel, or a distinctive word from the topic. Long sentences rarely work. Short terms with a person's name find the thread faster.

faq.question: Can Lazur send Slack messages for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur drafts and types text, and it answers questions about what is on screen. It does not click Send or operate Slack for you. You read the draft and press Return yourself.

faq.question: Does the Free plan keep all my Slack history?
faq.answer: No. Slack's pricing page says messages on the Free plan are searchable for 90 days. Upgrading gives access to the previous 12 months. Check the pricing page before you rely on search for older decisions.

faq.question: Which shortcut starts a huddle on Mac?
faq.answer: ⌘⇧H starts, joins, leaves, or ends a huddle. ⌘⇧Space mutes or unmutes while you are in one. Both come from Slack's keyboard shortcuts help page.

faq.question: Do I need Lazur to follow this page?
faq.answer: No. Every shortcut, menu path, and plan limit here works without Lazur. Lazur helps when you want a voice answer, a draft, or a point at a control you cannot find.
